name: Afghanistan
summary: A mountainous state founded as the Durrani Empire by Ahmad Shah Durrani in 1747. It was a buffer between the Russian and British empires, then went through monarchy, Soviet war, civil war and Taliban rule.

knownFor.label: Afghan carpets
knownFor.note: Hand-knotted wool carpets, often deep red.

knownFor.label: Buzkashi
knownFor.note: A horseback game where riders fight for a goat carcass.

knownFor.label: Ahmad Shah Durrani
knownFor.note: Founder of the Durrani Empire, seen as the father of Afghanistan.

location.value: Landlocked in Central and South Asia, between Iran, Pakistan and Central Asia; about 650,000 km².

terrain.value: The Hindu Kush mountains, high valleys and deserts in the south.

climate.value: Dry, with cold winters and hot summers.

resources.value: Farmland in valleys, lapis lazuli, copper and lithium deposits.

urbanisation.value: Kabul, Kandahar, Herat and Mazar-i-Sharif are the main cities.

disease.value: High child mortality; polio still present.

migration.value: Millions of refugees fled to Pakistan and Iran after 1979.

economicBase.value: Farming and herding; opium poppy was a major crop.

tradeRoutes.value: Old caravan routes between Central Asia, Iran and India.

inequality.value: Large gaps between cities and the countryside, and between men and women.

governmentType.value: Monarchy (1747–1973), republic, communist government, Islamic Emirate (1996–2001, and again since 2021).

keyRulers.value: Ahmad Shah Durrani. Dost Mohammad Khan. Amanullah Khan. Zahir Shah. Hamid Karzai.

succession.value: Royal succession, then coups, elections (2004–2019) and Taliban rule.

stability.value: Very unstable since 1973: coups, the Soviet war (1979–89), civil war and the US-led war (2001–21).

eliteConflict.value: Rivalries between ethnic and political factions.

majorWars.value: Anglo-Afghan Wars (1839–42, 1878–80, 1919); Soviet–Afghan War; War in Afghanistan (2001–21).

territoryChange.value: The Durand Line (1893) set the border with British India; still disputed by Afghanistan.

alliancesRivals.value: A buffer state in the “Great Game” between Russia and Britain.

scienceEducation.value: Low literacy; girls are banned from secondary school and university since 2021–22.

openness.value: Opened under Amanullah Khan (1920s), closed again in later periods.

communicationTransport.value: The Salang Tunnel (1964) through the Hindu Kush; few railways.

artsArchitecture.value: Carpets, Herat miniatures, the destroyed Buddhas of Bamiyan (2001).

socialStructure.value: Pashtun, Tajik, Hazara, Uzbek and other peoples.

dailyLife.value: Mud-brick houses in villages; bread (naan), rice (pulao), tea.

neighbours.value: Iran, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, China.

colonisation.value: Never formally colonised, though Britain controlled its foreign affairs until 1919.

riseSignals.value: Ahmad Shah Durrani united Afghan tribes after Nader Shah’s death (1747).

peakPeriod.value: The Durrani Empire in the 1750s–60s reached India.

outcome.value: Still in existence; the Taliban government is not widely recognised.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts documented; population and war figures are uncertain.
